meta.title: Portolan — An opinionated standard for cloud-native geospatial catalogs
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage, with no servers, no databases, and no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets a person or an agent read a catalog and query it directly. The standard sets the quality bar, a validator enforces it, tools make catalogs cheap to build, and a registry connects them into a network anyone can search.

hero.title: The future of spatial data
hero.description: Portolan is an opinionated standard for sharing geospatial data as cloud-native files on object storage, plus the tools that make it real. A Portolan catalog is a directory of open-format data described by structured <m>STAC</m> metadata, hosted on any S3-compatible bucket. No servers, no databases.

why.title: Spatial data infrastructure still assumes servers, databases, and specialists. Portolan doesn't.

open.title: Open and interoperable
open.description: Everything is open source under <m>Apache-2.0</m> and built on existing standards like <m>GeoParquet</m>, cloud-optimized GeoTIFF, and <m>STAC</m>. These formats work across DuckDB, BigQuery, Pandas, and desktop GIS like QGIS and ArcGIS, so your data stays useful with or without Portolan.

aiFirst.title: Readable by people and machines
aiFirst.description: Download portals and one-off APIs were built for one client at a time. A Portolan catalog describes itself in plain text and structured metadata, so a person or an agent can find the data and query it without a bespoke API to learn. The <link>Finland.SDI demo</link> shows an agent doing exactly that against a national SDI.

easy.title: Simple
easy.description: Traditional spatial data infrastructure needs databases, services, and staff to run them. A Portolan catalog is files in a bucket. Point the CLI at your data, convert, and push.

scalable.title: Scales with your storage
scalable.description: The same setup handles megabytes or terabytes. With no servers to run, scaling is your cloud provider's job, not yours.

lowCost.title: Low cost
lowCost.description: The whole budget is storage plus egress. Sharing public data should not take an operations team, and a popular dataset should not blow a budget. The <link>cost calculator</link> shows what your data would run.

sovereign.title: Sovereign
sovereign.description: The full stack can live inside your own jurisdiction. Host on AWS, GCS, Azure, MinIO, Hetzner, Scaleway, or any S3-compatible storage. No foreign vendor sits between your agency and its data.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Any input becomes cloud-native, legacy formats or new ones alike. Vectors turn into <m>GeoParquet</m>, rasters into <m>COG</m>, tiles into <m>PMTiles</m>.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: A <m>STAC</m> catalog describes every asset, so any <m>STAC</m> tool can read it.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Push the files to any S3-compatible storage, from AWS, GCS, and Azure to R2, MinIO, or Source Cooperative.

browse.title: Use
browse.description: Use it with standard geospatial tools like DuckDB, Sedona, and QGIS, or point an agent at the URL.

cli.title: With the CLI
cli.description: Install <m>portolan-cli</m>, then <m>init</m>, <m>add</m>, <m>check</m>, and <m>push</m>. The CLI converts your files and generates the catalog.

claude.title: With Claude
claude.description: Install the Portolan skill in Claude Code and point it at your data. It handles conversion, metadata, and publishing. Agents excel at CLIs and text files, so non-experts can publish too.
